blurb: The clay army that guards the tomb of China's first emperor.

facts.h: Found by farmers digging a well
facts.t: In March 1974 farmers near Xi'an dug into pieces of clay soldiers. Archaeologists now think there are about 8,000 figures, each with its own face. Most are still underground.

src.n: Wikipedia: Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor

facts.t: Qin Shi Huang's own burial mound has never been dug. The historian Sima Qian wrote that it held rivers of mercury; tests of the soil have found unusually high mercury.
